spectrum_quality_justification: Spectrum shows a spectacular bright narrow emission line at 4767 Å (amplitude +6.1, the dominant feature) and a very bright narrow emission complex around 6072 Å. Continuum is well-detected across the full range. However, many CWT-detected features have near-zero amplitude (0.000) and are indistinguishable from the local noise floor — these are pure CWT phantom detections.

global_issues: Blue edge (<4000 Å) shows elevated noise and throughput collapse. Features here require extra scrutiny.

OH airglow zone (>7800 Å) shows dense skyline residuals. Features at 7932.8, 7983.2, 7994.4, 8301.6, 8367.2, 8468.0, 8484.8, 8520.0, 8616.0, 8645.6, 8832.0, 9051.2 may be contaminated. OH forest is especially dense beyond 9000 Å.
OI airglow at 5577.3, 6300.3, 6363.8 Å may contaminate narrow emission features in the visible band — no features in the matrix fall within ±10 Å of these positions.
Many CWT-detected features have amplitude 0.000 and are pure phantom detections — the CWT pipeline appears to have over-fitted noise across much of the spectrum.
The spectrum is dominated by a very bright narrow emission at 4767 Å and a bright narrow emission complex around 6072 Å. Most other claimed features are at or near the noise floor.

doublet_verdicts.notes: Both components are real narrow emission peaks confirmed via Step 3. However, the ratio a/b=1.00 is inconsistent with [O III] (expected a/b ≈ 0.33). [O III]a is as bright as [O III]b when it should be ~3× fainter. Both should be KEEP (real peaks) but the ratio anomaly suggests possible blending or misidentification.

Ca K_abs at 3932.8 is a real absorption trough (trough minimum slightly offset at 3931.2). Ca H_abs at 3961.6 is NOT real — flux is rising through this region, no absorption trough. The 'doublet' is a chance alignment of one real feature with a noise detection.
